stories.title: Oregon, Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok's sexual deepfakes
stories.summary: Oregon and Virginia's attorneys general filed separate lawsuits accusing SpaceX of violating consumer protection laws by letting Grok generate sexual deepfakes, including alleged child sexual abuse material and revenge porn.
stories.more: The complaints, filed Monday, accuse SpaceX of ignoring industry-standard safeguards while falsely promoting the safety of X and Grok. Virginia's filing specifically accuses Elon Musk of willful violations. X has said every Grok output is screened, but the state attorneys general argue Grok is still producing CSAM and non-consensual sexual imagery. The lawsuits add to mounting legal pressure on SpaceX over Grok's content moderation.

stories.title: Megaspeed, tied to Huang scandal, nears US blacklist
stories.summary: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal and previously led by Alice Huang, appears headed for a U.S. blacklist barring American firms from doing business with it without a special license.
stories.more: The action would restrict companies from transacting with Megaspeed unless they obtain a special government license. Megaspeed was previously led by Alice Huang and has been linked to the scandal that led to Jensen Huang's temporary resignation from Nvidia. Details on the timing and scope of the blacklisting have not been disclosed.

stories.title: AI data centers' power demand complicates UN climate talks
stories.summary: Power-hungry AI data centers added friction to the UN's COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, as delegates tried to reconcile electrifying the global economy with surging data center energy demand.
stories.more: The clean energy transition depends on electrifying the broader economy, but that goal is colliding with the rapid growth of electricity-hungry AI data centers. Delegates at COP31 grappled with this tension throughout the summit, which closed in a chaotic and unsatisfying manner. The excerpt does not specify what, if any, agreements were reached on data center energy use.

stories.title: OpenAI scientist proposes perplexity as shared AI safety limit metric
stories.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki released internal perplexity scores across the entire GPT series, including an unreleased model, and is urging rival labs to adopt shared capability limits before safety controls erode.
stories.more: Pachocki's disclosure marks the first time OpenAI has shared perplexity figures spanning the full GPT lineage, including a model beyond the current generation. The data reportedly shows that core capabilities emerge at surprisingly precise thresholds as perplexity improves. Pachocki is pushing to establish perplexity as an industry-wide progress metric. He is also urging competing labs to agree on shared limits, warning that future AI systems could outpace safety checks.

The philosopher's critique challenges the premise behind Anthropic's approach to model sentience and moral consideration. Further specifics of the rebuttal were not included in the excerpt.

stories.title: Motion Mamba 2.0 targets long-horizon humanoid motion control
stories.summary: Researchers introduced Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based diffusion architecture for generating long-horizon, real-time controllable motion for interactive animation and humanoid robotics.
stories.more: The paper targets a limitation of existing autoregressive diffusion motion methods: bounded attention caches restrict access to distant history, while repeated denoising adds inference overhead. Motion Mamba 2.0 integrates a root-body diffusion architecture to address this. It aims to let agents respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while already moving. Further benchmark results were not included in the excerpt.

stories.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion automates rigging for diverse 3D game assets
stories.summary: A new system, 3AGameFactory-Motion, performs agentic rigging and complex motion generation for diverse 3D assets, paired with a new benchmark covering six morphology categories.
stories.more: Existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions, the paper notes. The authors introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories using instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. The system uses large language models as part of its rigging and motion pipeline. Comparisons against other approaches on the new benchmark were not detailed in the excerpt.

stories.summary: Google DeepMind used teams of AI agents combined with formal verification to discover faster quantum algorithms, targeting applications in fusion research and chemistry.
stories.more: The approach pairs agent teams with formal verification methods to search for and validate improved quantum algorithms. DeepMind highlights potential applications in fusion research and chemistry simulation. Specific performance gains over existing algorithms were not detailed in the excerpt.

stories.title: Self-distillation framework teaches video foresight reasoning
stories.summary: Researchers proposed an on-policy self-distillation framework that trains vision-language models to anticipate future video events, using only unlabeled past-future video pairs as a self-supervised signal.
stories.more: Video foresight reasoning requires models to predict future events or next actions from observed video. Prior approaches fit future captions, rationales, or visual states but relied on annotations or large external models for supervision, limiting scalability. This method instead turns past-future video pairs into a natural self-supervised signal without extra annotation or LLM support. Further evaluation details were not included in the excerpt.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship for AI-driven pull request review
stories.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Ship, which lets Claude review, fix, and approve pull requests on its own, building on its existing code review feature to help engineers manage AI-generated code.
stories.more: The Claude Ship product extends Claude's existing code review capabilities so the model can handle routine approvals as well as reviews and fixes. Anthropic positions it as a way to reduce bottlenecks created by the growing volume of AI-generated code. Engineers had previously been able to use Claude to review and suggest fixes, but not to approve changes outright. It was announced alongside other new Claude AI features aimed at software engineers shipping code.

stories.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0 adds Datasette Agent integration
stories.summary: Simon Willison released datasette-charts 0.2a0, a charting plugin for Datasette that now integrates with Datasette Agent so users can ask for a chart in chat and have it generated automatically.
stories.more: The plugin lets a chat interface generate charts using the same underlying suggestion and generation tools as the standalone plugin. Willison demonstrated it on agent.datasette.io, where visitors can sign in with GitHub to try it. The demo shows prompting Datasette Agent to chart sqlite-utils download statistics over time. The plugin builds on a charting feature Willison introduced the previous day.

stories.title: datasette-agent 0.7a1 improves iframe panel navigation
stories.summary: Simon Willison released datasette-agent 0.7a1, adding an iframe side panel that chat sessions can open and navigate, with improved support for fragment-hash based navigation across Datasette plugins.
stories.more: The update lets chat sessions open an iframe side panel and then navigate that panel to different pages. Navigation now works via fragment hashes, improving integration with other Datasette plugins that update fragment hashes as users interact with them. Willison built this release partly to fix bugs affecting the newly released datasette-charts 0.2a0 plugin.

stories.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux designed to help teams protect running systems while they roll out security patches.
stories.more: Shirudo aims to reduce the window of exposure between a vulnerability's discovery and when a patch is fully deployed, by protecting systems still running unpatched code. The tool is open source and targets Linux systems. Further technical details on how Shirudo works were not included in the excerpt.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after political pressure
stories.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO days after his resignation over an alleged affair, following reported phone calls from President Trump urging the board to bring him back. Employees welcomed Huang at headquarters, and Nvidia's stock rose on the news.
stories.more: Huang resigned on November 12th amid scrutiny over an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, but Nvidia's board reversed course and reinstated him within weeks. Techcrunch reported that President Trump personally called into a Nvidia board meeting to advocate for Huang's return, and Trump later told CNBC he had "convinced" the board. Huang was greeted by employees at Nvidia's headquarters as a hero and told staff he intends to be "a better CEO the second time around." Nvidia's stock price rose following the reinstatement. Commentators were split: some framed it as a sign of impunity for powerful executives, while others noted unresolved questions about the episode remain.

stories.title: Supertake raises $20M to turn market predictions into AI-run portfolios
stories.summary: Startup Supertake raised $20 million for a platform that turns users' market predictions into stock portfolios managed by AI agents, without requiring them to pick individual stocks.
stories.more: Supertake's pitch is to let people back their market views with money without needing to select stocks directly. The startup uses AI agents to translate those predictions into actual portfolios. Details on investors and valuation were not disclosed in the announcement.

stories.title: Anthropic's compute spending pushes xAI toward renting over building
stories.summary: Anthropic's roughly $3.1 billion monthly compute spending, alongside Google's $800 million, is reportedly pushing xAI (SpaceXSI) to rent compute to competitors rather than build its own AI infrastructure.
stories.more: Since May, SpaceXSI has rented compute to competitors including Anthropic and Google while scaling back its own AI projects, according to the New York Times. Anthropic reportedly pays about $3.1 billion a month and Google about $800 million for that compute. After SpaceXSI's June IPO, the company disbanded its 60-person Grok Imagine team as part of broader cuts. The report frames the shift as a rent-over-build strategy driven by rivals' compute demand.

Financial terms beyond the reported $7.5 billion price were not disclosed.

stories.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4 with a loop transformer architecture
stories.summary: Chinese AI lab Z.ai released GLM-5.4, its first model built on a looped transformer architecture that reruns weight-shared layers multiple times to refine hidden states without adding parameters.
stories.more: In a standard transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass; GLM-5.4's loop transformer instead runs a group of weight-shared layers for multiple iterations per pass. Z.ai describes this as a way to get a deeper effective network without increasing parameter count. The release is aimed at generalized coding tasks. Further benchmark details were not included in the excerpt.

stories.title: OpenAI makes GPT-6.2 Sol the default ChatGPT model
stories.summary: OpenAI is rolling out GPT-6.2 Sol as the new default model in ChatGPT's chat tab worldwide, with better handling of complex questions, web search, and images.
stories.more: In OpenAI's internal tests, image understanding accuracy jumped from 47.4 to 71.7 percent with the new model. GPT-6.2 Sol also follows difficult instructions correctly 78.1 percent of the time, per those tests. OpenAI says the model sticks to safety policies more consistently than its predecessor. The rollout applies to ChatGPT's chat tab globally.

It also sticks to safety policies more consistently. The article OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably appeared first on The Decoder .

stories.title: Google Search's AI Mode adds Personal Intelligence from Drive, Wallet

stories.more: The update extends AI Mode's Personal Intelligence capability to also tap Google Drive and Google Wallet, in addition to other Google services. It also reaches the Gemini app. Google frames the change as using data already within its ecosystem to make Search results more tailored to each user. The company did not detail specific new query types this enables or a rollout timeline.

stories.title: Ladybird browser ships its first alpha release
stories.summary: The Ladybird browser project shipped its first alpha release, an independent browser built largely from scratch with its own HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and layout engines.
stories.more: Ladybird implements most of its own core components rather than relying on an existing browser engine. It still uses some external libraries, including HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite. The rest of the browser is original code or carried over from Ladybird's predecessor project, SerenityOS. The alpha marks a milestone for a project aiming to build a modern browser largely from first principles.
